newsitem.title: JAPAN: Cabin to close 70 shops, cut work force.
newsitem.headline: Cabin to close 70 shops, cut work force.

text.p: Japanese women's wear retailer Cabin Co Ltd said on Tuesday it would close about 70 shops in the next year which it believed unlikely to return to profit.
It currently has a total of 396 shops, all in Japan.
The company said in a statement that the closures, to be implemented in the business year to February 1998, would result in a special loss of about 460 million yen for the year.

The closure would cut the company's annual sales by 4.3 billion yen. It would also cut the number of workers and part-timers by around 280, while reducing annual labour costs by 670 million yen and operating costs by 900 million yen.
Cabin said it would also introduce an early retirement scheme as a part of its overall restructuring.
Earlier this month, the company forecast a parent net loss of 2.17 billion yen for the year to February 1997, which would be the fourth successive year of such losses.
